messages:
marta: hitting noisy SLO alert for 'log-query-latency' — Grafana shows a big 95th spike for Loki queries that pull GPU allocation logs from us-west-2. Anyone see correlation IDs in Kibana for slow queries? need trace -> query mapping

andrew: paste the panel link and an example trace_id if you have one. usually X-Request-ID or trace_id in nginx/API gateway. can try correlate with jaeger.

marta: panel: https://grafana.redwood/logs/d/abc123
example req_id=01f23a9b-cf3e-4d2f
sample Loki query i ran (slow ~6s for 1h range):
```loki
{job=\"loki-gpu-logs\", region=\"us-west-2\"} | json | req_id=\"01f23a9b-cf3e-4d2f\" | line_format "{ts} {msg}"
```

dave: could be cross-region shipping. we're funneling via central s3 -> ingesters in us-east. queries become fanout across many ingesters if the series cardinality is high. check distributor and ingester latencies: loki_distributor_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"loki\"} and loki_ingester_* metrics.

kai: also looks like alert is noisy because rule aggregates across tenants. current SLO is raw p95 across all tenants. i'd exclude dev/staging tenants and use rate() with a 5m window and a 15m eval to reduce flapping.

andrew: practical tip: use label filters + prefix indexing where possible. e.g.
`{job=\"loki-gpu-logs\", tenant=\"prod\"} |~ \"trace_id=\\\"(?P<tr>[^\\\"]+)\\\"\"`
this scans far fewer series than region-only queries. avoid wide regexes on high-card fields.

marta: good call. dave — can you check ingester CPU and series overlap? andrew — can you add a short runbook snippet for query tuning?

dave: on it. note: we bumped loki-ingester replicas yesterday, but gpu logs retention is 30d and cardinality is high (pod, container, model_id). consider downsampling older logs or moving to archive to reduce active series.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 Loki query SLO noise — https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0423 (assigned to eng-sre)

kai: proposed alert change:
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(loki_distributor_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant!~\"dev|staging\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 1.5
```
Eval for 15m, suppress for known analytics windows.

andrew: adding runbook gist with example queries + trace correlation methods: https://gist.github.com/andrew/xyz (will include how to pull X-Request-ID from nginx and join with jaeger)

marta: thanks — i'll test tenant filter and re-run the slow query. if latency persists i'll capture full jaeger trace_id and paste here.

dave: FYI i'll also scope expensive consumers via per-tenant dashboards and suggest per-tenant query quotas. might need to throttle heavy ad-hoc analytics queries from internal teams.

marta: update: tenant filter dropped p95 from ~2.1s -> ~0.65s. opening PR to change alert thresholds and add suppression for analytics windows.

obs-bot: PR opened: #1874 update loki SLO alert (linked to INC-2026-0423)

andrew: nice. add runbook note: prefer label+prefix filtering, avoid expensive regex, and fallback to read-replica for big ad-hoc scans.

kai: also consider routing heavy queries to an in-region read-replica cluster to avoid central fanout and cross-region latency.

marta: adding that to follow-up RFC. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
